Advanced technology, a world-class clinical development organization, and state-of-the-art facilities: these and other resources empower us to innovate and touch the lives of more and more patients. It’s our work, our passion, and our legacy. We invite you to join us.
  
  
**Hybrid:** 3-days per week on-site
  
Employee Value Proposition
  
​​​​​​At Taiho Oncology, the compassion we practice for our patients extends to our team, empowering and motivating them to do their best work for those who need it most. This is an exciting opportunity to lead critical Quality systems in a dynamic, collaborative, and global cross-functional environment.
  
  
**Position Summary:**  
​​​​​​​​​The Director, QA Ops – Document, Training & Records Management is responsible for the strategy, governance, and execution of Taiho Oncology’s controlled document management, GxP training management, archival, and records-retention programs. This position leads the team responsible for day-to-day activities in MasterControl and establishes scalable processes, system capabilities, and governance that support current operations and Taiho’s future business plans. The Director partners with Quality, functional leaders, Information Technology, system owners, affiliates, and global stakeholders to maintain compliant, efficient, and inspection-ready programs.
  
  
**Performance Objectives:**  
**​​​​Strategy, Governance and Leadership:**  

* Develop and execute the long-term strategy and operating model for controlled document management, GxP training management, archival, and records retention.
* Translate Taiho’s future plans into scalable processes, systems, governance, resources, and program roadmaps.
* Establish policies, standards, performance measures, risk controls, and continuous-improvement priorities and provide recommendations to senior management.
* Lead harmonization and standardization of document and training practices across TOI and applicable affiliates and global stakeholders.
* Manage, coach, and develop the team responsible for document, training, archival, and records-management activities; maintain clear roles, capacity, cross-training, succession planning, and business continuity.

**MasterControl and Quality System Oversight:**  

* Provide business ownership, strategic direction, and governance for MasterControl document and training capabilities.
* Oversee administration of document workflows, courses, curricula, assignments, job codes, user accounts, metadata, effective dates, access, archival status, and related records.
* Partner with Information Technology and validation stakeholders on enhancements, upgrades, integrations, access controls, user acceptance testing, Computer System Assurance documentation, and maintenance of the validated state.
* Evaluate and implement capabilities needed to align MasterControl with business growth, affiliate integration, data integrity, inspection readiness, and future quality-system plans.
* Ensure procedures, user guidance, training materials, reports, and support mechanisms remain current and effective.

**Controlled Document Management:**  

* Oversee the lifecycle management of controlled policies, standard operating procedures, work instructions, forms, guidance documents, and other GxP documents from creation through retirement and archival.
* Establish standards for templates, numbering, naming, metadata, review and approval, effective dates, revision history, periodic review, document relationships, distribution, and supersession.
* Ensure controlled documents receive appropriate Quality and administrative review and that document owners resolve quality, workflow, implementation, and timeliness issues.
* Lead periodic assessment and cleanup of the controlled-document environment, including obsolete, duplicate, or floating documents and attachments.
* Provide document-management leadership and evidence support during audits, inspections, due diligence, and compliance reviews.

**GxP Training Management:**  

* Establish the strategy and governance framework for GxP training across TOI and applicable affiliates.
* Ensure training requirements, curricula, courses, job codes, assignments, and records are aligned with job responsibilities, controlled documents, organizational changes, and compliance obligations.
* Oversee onboarding, role changes, transfers, leaves of absence, and separation processes as they affect training requirements and records.
* Ensure required training is assigned, completed, tracked, documented, reported, and retained; monitor compliance and escalate material risks.
* Oversee new-hire Quality training, document creator/revisor training, instructor-led training, read-and-understand activities, assessments, and other approved training methods.
* Lead improvements that strengthen training effectiveness, learner experience, role alignment, reporting, and inspection readiness.

**Archival and Records Retention:**  

* Develop and oversee the strategy for identification, transfer, storage, protection, retrieval, retention, disposition, and migration of applicable quality records.
* Partner with Legal, Information Technology, Records Management, functional stakeholders, and Quality Assurance to establish and maintain appropriate retention requirements and controls.
* Ensure electronic and physical records, as applicable, remain authentic, complete, readable, secure, traceable, accessible, and retrievable throughout the retention period.
* Identify and remediate risks involving legacy records, decentralized repositories, inconsistent practices, obsolete formats, or system migrations.
* Maintain inspection readiness; support audits and regulatory inspections; lead remediation, CAPA, and risk-management activities related to assigned processes.
* Establish and report metrics for document timeliness, training compliance, overdue activities, processing volume, archival status, system performance, and program risk.
* Perform other related duties as assigned.

**Education/Certification Requirements:**  

* ​​​​​​​​Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, quality, regulatory affairs, information management, business, or a related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**  

* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or other regulated life-sciences industry.
* Significant experience in Quality Assurance, controlled document management, GxP training, archival, records retention, and regulated quality systems.
* Demonstrated experience leading teams and complex cross-functional programs; experience supporting regulatory inspections and audits required.
* Experience with MasterControl document and training modules, validated computerized systems, and system implementations, upgrades, or migrations strongly preferred.
* Comprehensive knowledge of GxP quality-system principles and regulated document, training, archival, records-retention, and data-integrity practices.
* Demonstrated ability to establish strategy, governance, and future-state plans while ensuring effective and timely operational execution.
* Strong people leadership, coaching, delegation, succession planning, stakeholder management, and change-leadership skills.
* Strong project, program, risk, and regulatory management abilities, including development of metrics, management reporting, and sustainable process improvements.
* Excellent written, verbal, presentation, analytical, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and communicate effectively at all organizational levels.
* Sound judgment and proven ability to define problems, analyze data, assess risk, manage competing priorities, and implement compliant, scalable solutions.
* Highly developed organizational skills, attention to detail, accountability, and commitment to collaboration and inspection readiness.

**About CAMP Systems:**  
At CAMP Systems, we are the trusted leader in aircraft compliance and health management, proudly serving the global business aviation industry. With over 20,000 aircraft and 33,000 engines supported on our cutting-edge platforms, and partnerships with more than 1,300 maintenance facilities and parts suppliers worldwide, we’re shaping the future of aviation technology. Since our founding in 1968, we’ve grown to a dynamic team of 1,600+ employees across 14 locations globally—all united by a passion for innovation and excellence.

**Our Mission & Vision:**  
We connect the aviation industry through smart technology to make flight safer and more efficient, driving the future of aviation with intelligence and exceptional customer experiences.

**Our Values & Excellence Mindset:**  
We are customer obsessed, trust-driven, owners of our work, stronger together, constantly curious, and boldly innovative.

  

**What You Will Experience in This Role:**

The Director – Quality Assurance drives quality across CAMP's Aircraft Health Management business and provides quality oversight for data and process quality concerns. The role owns the QMS, the internal audit program, and the full quality escape lifecycle, and serves as CAMP's quality voice with OEMs, regulators, and key customers. The right candidate combines deep aviation maintenance knowledge with a disciplined, data-driven approach to compliance and continuous improvement.

This is a high-visibility leadership role reporting to the Vice President, Aviation Health Management Operations. The Director partners with senior leaders across a global organization and will build on an established quality program: strengthening the QMS, deepening OEM and customer confidence, and scaling quality practices as AHM grows.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategy & Leadership**

* Own and lead quality strategy across the full Aircraft Health Management organization, spanning maintenance tracking and engine health monitoring services, aligned with CAMP's business objectives.
* Serve as the escalation point for quality complaints from customer-facing, maintenance compliance, engine health monitoring, flight scheduling, and inventory functions.
* Partner with senior management and departmental leaders to embed quality methodologies across the organization and lead the associated change management.
* Own the quality budget, resource plan, and tooling (QMS, audit, and corrective action platforms), and build the succession pipeline for the quality team.

**Quality Management System & Certification**

* Own the Quality Management System (QMS) and quality SOPs, driving continuous improvement and ensuring processes meet strict regulatory and OEM requirements.
* Maintain ISO 9001 (or higher) certification for the engine health monitoring business, serving as external certification audit lead and ensuring ongoing audit readiness.
* Lead QMS management review with executive leadership, setting risk-based quality objectives and ensuring consistent QMS implementation (document control, competency records, data integrity) across all AHM locations in North America, Europe, and India.

**Audit & Compliance**

* Own the internal audit program end to end, including audit planning, execution, reporting, and the selection, training, and management of internal auditors.
* Host and manage OEM, customer, and third-party audits, driving findings to timely closure.

**Quality Escapes & Corrective Action**

* Manage all quality escapes from intake through investigation, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and verification of effectiveness, with clear accountability to customers and OEM partners.
* Define and report corrective action performance metrics (e.g., escape rate, time to containment, on-time closure, recurrence) with clear thresholds and escalation paths.

**OEM & Customer Engagement**

* Facilitate and chair weekly, monthly, and quarterly strategic OEM meetings covering quality trends, KPI compliance, and corrective action status.
* Serve as primary quality liaison to OEM partners, regulatory bodies, and high-profile customers and large fleet operators under significant OEM contracts.
* Facilitate weekly, monthly, and quarterly quality reviews with senior management and functional leaders, translating escape, audit, and customer feedback data into trends and strategic quality initiatives.

**Continuous Improvement & Team Leadership**

* Lead process improvement using Lean Six Sigma methods, mentoring teams and driving measurable reductions in escapes, rework, and risk.
* Maintain an executive quality scorecard (customer feedback, escapes, audit results, corrective action performance) to drive data-based decisions.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of four, setting priorities and fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and collaboration.
* Partner with AHM operations, training, and product leaders to ensure analyst competency, training effectiveness, and quality readiness for new products, processes, and teams.

  

**You have:**

* Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.
* Minimum of 10 years of proven leadership experience in the aviation or aerospace sector, with senior quality assurance experience preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of aviation maintenance and its regulatory requirements (FAA, EASA, and OEM requirements). Hands-on aviation maintenance experience may offset formal credentials.
* Experience managing quality escapes, investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action programs.
* Experience owning or managing a QMS in a regulated environment, with working knowledge of ISO 9001 (AS9100 familiarity a plus).
* Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn quality data into executive-level metrics, insights, and recommendations.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to build relationships with OEMs, customers, and leaders at all levels of the organization.
* Strategic thinking with a strong focus on results and the ability to manage complex projects and initiatives.
* Ability to lead across a multi-site, multi-region team; willingness to travel to CAMP offices, OEM, and customer sites as needed.

**Nice to have:**

* Certified ISO 9001 Internal/External Auditor (or equivalent lead auditor certification) with hands-on audit experience.
* Six Sigma Black Belt, with demonstrated process improvement results.
* Quality manager certification (e.g., ASQ CQM) or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) is a bonus.
* Experience working with large OEM contracts and high-profile customers or large fleet operators.
* Experience in aircraft maintenance tracking, engine trend monitoring, or other SaaS/data-driven service environments.

  

**Why Work at CAMP?**

Join a culture where your ideas matter, your impact is real, and your growth is supported. Be part of a team reimagining the future of aviation.

CAMP is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer – vets/disabled

CAMP is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, please contact hr@campsystems.com (mailto:hr@campsystems.com).

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status EEO.

Equal Opportunity Employer  
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

Join Gilead and help create possible, together.
  
  
**Job Description**

**EXAMPLE RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* **Set the global Digital Quality strategy and roadmap**
  + Define the target state, strategic themes, capability model, and multi-year roadmap for Digital Quality.

  + Lead market scans, demonstrations, proofs of concept, pilots, supplier due diligence, and fit-gap assessments.
  + Recommend whether to adopt, configure, integrate, scale, defer, or reject proposed solutions based on documented evidence.

  + Define decision rights, design principles, architecture guardrails, stage gates, risk criteria, and governance forums for the Digital Quality portfolio.
  + Apply risk-based lifecycle assurance based on intended use and process risk, including requirements, supplier evidence, testing, traceability, release, change control, periodic review, and retirement.

  + Provide Quality leadership through product selection, design, configuration, testing, deployment, stabilization, and continuous improvement.

  + Monitor solution performance, incidents, compliance signals, user feedback, benefits, and emerging risks throughout the lifecycle.

Momentive Technologies applies advanced materials science to design and manufacture ultra-high-performance quartz materials, quartz crucibles, and ceramic products that are vital to a variety of high-growth end markets, including the silicon and compound semiconductor industries, electronics, and aerospace components. **Director Global Quality**

The Director, Global Quality is a highly visible leadership role responsible for shaping and advancing quality strategy across our global organization. Serving as a trusted advisor to the Executive Leadership Team, this individual will provide insight into quality performance, requirements, risks, and opportunities while driving greater consistency and excellence across operations in the United States, Germany, South Korea, China, and Japan.

* Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, Technology, and Commercial leadership to integrate quality requirements and risk management into sourcing decisions, manufacturing strategy, new products, process changes, and capacity expansion.

existing_roles.description:
**About Tutor**
---------------

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**The Role**
------------

As Head of Technical Operations, you’ll own manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations. We build hundreds of robots a year today and need to build a lot more. You’ll own how we get there, including the teams, suppliers and facilities, and work closely with engineering along the way.

You’ll report to the CTO. This is an onsite role in Watertown, MA.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

* Scaling production from hundreds of robots a year to many more
* Manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service and robot operations
* The teams, suppliers and facilities behind production
* A close partnership with engineering

**Requirements**
----------------

* Ran manufacturing or operations at a company that builds complex hardware in volume
* Built an operations function and hired the people who run it
* Been responsible for a fleet of products in the field, including service and support
* Sets clear targets and hires well
* Comfortable on a factory floor

**Nice to have:**

* Robotics, or other products that combine hardware and software
* Experience with contract manufacturers
* Experience with quality systems

**What to Expect**
------------------

We want you to know exactly what to expect. Here’s what our interview process typically looks like:

* **Recruiter interview:** A conversation with a member of our Recruiting team about your background and what you’re looking for.
* **Hiring manager interview:** A deeper conversation with the hiring manager about the role and your experience.
* **Onsite:** A presentation with the team, 1:1s with key team members, and a tour of our facility.

Some roles include additional steps, such as a technical assessment or take-home exercise. If yours does, we’ll let you know up front. Throughout the process, we’ll aim to keep you updated at each step as quickly as possible.

**Why Tutor?**
--------------

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**Benefits**
------------

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.

existing_roles.title: Plant Manager
existing_roles.description:
**Compensation Range:**

$122,800 - $204,600

**Plant Manager**

Department: Operations / Manufacturing

Reports To: Director of Operations

Direct Reports: Production Managers, Facilities Manager, and other assigned manufacturing leadership

Scope: Three manufacturing buildings / multi-product HVAC manufacturing operation

**Position**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, and day-to-day execution of manufacturing operations across three buildings within a large HVAC manufacturing facility. This position provides hands-on leadership to ensure the plant safely produces high-quality products on schedule, at the required volume and cost, while developing a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

The Plant Manager is responsible for coordinating production activities across multiple manufacturing processes and buildings, including assembly, sheet metal fabrication, welding, piping/refrigeration, testing, material flow, and final product completion.

The successful candidate will establish clear operating standards, drive cross-functional accountability, develop manufacturing leadership, remove operational constraints, and ensure the plant has the people, processes, equipment, and infrastructure required to support current production and future growth.

This position is expected to be highly visible on the manufacturing floor and serves as the primary operational leader responsible for translating business objectives into daily execution.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Plant Leadership & Operational Execution**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for manufacturing operations across all three buildings.
* Establish daily, weekly, and monthly operating priorities aligned with business requirements.
* Ensure production plans are executed safely, efficiently, and according to customer commitments.
* Maintain strong communication and coordination between buildings and manufacturing departments.
* Establish clear ownership and accountability for production performance.
* Lead daily plant operating reviews and ensure corrective actions are completed.
* Identify and remove constraints affecting throughput, capacity, quality, or delivery.
* Maintain appropriate production capacity, staffing, equipment, and infrastructure to support business growth.
* Ensure standardized processes are consistently followed across all buildings.
* Maintain a strong management presence on the manufacturing floor.

**2. Production Management**

* Lead Production Managers and ensure effective management of production personnel.
* Establish production priorities based on customer demand, capacity, material availability, and schedule requirements.
* Ensure production schedules are achieved while balancing labor, equipment, materials, and testing capacity.
* Monitor production flow from fabrication through final assembly and testing.
* Develop and maintain effective production metrics and visual management systems.
* Identify bottlenecks and implement corrective actions to improve throughput.
* Ensure appropriate escalation processes are in place when production performance is at risk.
* Coordinate production activities between the three buildings to maximize overall plant capacity.

**3. Safety, Environmental & Compliance**

* Establish safety as the facility’s highest operational priority.
* Partner with EHS leadership to maintain a strong safety culture across all three buildings.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental regulations, company requirements, and applicable industry standards.
* Drive accountability for safe work practices at all levels of the organization.
* Ensure timely investigation and corrective action following incidents, near misses, and unsafe conditions.
* Support programs designed to reduce injuries, ergonomic risks, environmental impacts, and workplace hazards.
* Ensure employees receive appropriate safety training and understand their responsibilities.

**4. Quality**

* Partner with Quality leadership to ensure products meet customer, engineering, and company requirements.
* Establish accountability for first-time quality and defect prevention.
* Drive reduction of scrap, rework, warranty issues, and production defects.
* Ensure quality issues are rapidly escalated and contained.
* Support root-cause analysis and corrective-action processes.
* Promote quality at the source rather than relying on downstream inspection.
* Maintain compliance with the plant's quality management system and ISO requirements.

**5. Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead the implementation and sustainability of Lean Manufacturing Principles throughout all three buildings.
* Establish a culture of continuous improvement and employee involvement.
* Drive 5S, visual management, standardized work, problem solving, waste elimination, and flow improvements.
* Support Value Stream Mapping and improvement of end-to-end product flow.
* Establish measurable improvement targets for productivity, quality, delivery, inventory, and cost.
* Partner with Lean/Manufacturing Engineering leadership to prioritize improvement projects based on business impact.
* Ensure Lean improvements are sustained through management systems and standard work.
* Develop frontline leaders capable of independently identifying and solving operational problems.

**6. People Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Develop a high-performing manufacturing leadership team.
* Establish clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
* Coach and develop Production Managers, Supervisors, and other manufacturing leaders.
* Identify organizational capability gaps and work with Human Resources to develop staffing and development plans.
* Support workforce planning and hiring activities necessary to meet production requirements.
* Establish effective onboarding and training processes for new employees.
* Develop succession plans for key manufacturing positions.
* Promote employee engagement, teamwork, ownership, and accountability.
* Address performance issues promptly and consistently.

**7. Capacity & Business Growth**

* Develop manufacturing capacity plans to support current and future customer demand.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Finance, Materials, and other functions to identify capacity requirements.
* Evaluate labor, equipment, floor space, testing, utilities, and infrastructure requirements.
* Support capital planning and justification for new equipment and facility improvements.
* Ensure new production areas and buildings are effectively integrated into the overall manufacturing system.
* Develop ramp-up plans for new products, programs, and production transfers.
* Ensure the plant can scale production without compromising safety, quality, or delivery performance.

**8. Cross-Functional Leadership**

Work closely with:

* Director of Operations
* Production
* Materials
* Production Planning
* Logistics
* Quality
* EHS
* Lean / Manufacturing Engineering
* Facilities
* Maintenance
* Engineering
* Finance
* Human Resources
* Supply Chain
* Sales / Customer teams

Ensure cross-functional issues are identified early, assigned to the appropriate owner, and driven to resolution.

**9. Facilities, Equipment & Infrastructure**

* Partner with Facilities and Maintenance leadership to ensure buildings, utilities, production equipment, cranes, test infrastructure, and other critical assets support production requirements.
* Establish preventive and predictive maintenance expectations.
* Ensure critical production equipment has appropriate contingency plans.
* Support capital equipment selection, installation, commissioning, and production launch.
* Ensure facility expansion projects are integrated into manufacturing operations with minimal disruption to production.

**10. Performance Management & Accountability**

Establish and maintain a plant operating system based on measurable performance.

Key performance indicators should include:

Safety

* Recordable incident rate
* Lost-time incidents
* Near misses
* Safety observations
* Corrective-action closure

Quality

* First-pass yield
* Scrap
* Rework
* Customer defects
* Warranty / quality escapes

Delivery

* On-time delivery
* Schedule attainment
* Production attainment
* Manufacturing lead time
* Test-bay utilization / throughput

Productivity

* Labor productivity
* Units per labor hour
* OEE where applicable
* Direct labor efficiency
* Throughput

Cost

* Manufacturing cost
* Labor variance
* Scrap cost
* Overtime
* Cost of poor quality

Lean

* 5S performance
* Kaizen completion
* Standard work compliance
* Improvement savings
* Value-stream performance

The Plant Manager will ensure performance is reviewed routinely and that corrective actions have clearly identified owners and due dates.

**Leadership Expectations**

The Plant Manager is expected to:

* Lead from the floor rather than from the office.
* Establish a culture of accountability without creating a culture of blame.
* Make decisions based on facts and data.
* Escalate issues early rather than allowing problems to become emergencies.
* Develop leaders instead of personally solving every problem.
* Maintain a strong focus on safety and quality while driving production.
* Create alignment between the three buildings rather than allowing them to operate as independent plants.
* Establish consistent standards and expectations across the operation.
* Communicate clearly with employees, leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Demonstrate urgency while maintaining disciplined problem solving.
* Build an organization capable of supporting significant business growth.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field preferred.
* 7+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 3+ years of plant or multi-department manufacturing management experience.
* Experience managing large manufacturing organizations, multiple production areas, and facilities.
* Experience in HVAC, refrigeration, industrial equipment, sheet metal, welding, assembly, or related manufacturing strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience managing significant production growth or plant expansion.
* Strong understanding of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Demonstrated experience managing safety, quality, delivery, and cost performance.
* Strong financial and business acumen.
* Experience developing and leading supervisors and managers.
* Strong communication and organizational skills.
* Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth manufacturing environment.

**Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality**

**Location:** Lakewood, Ohio  
**Company:** Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company  
**Employment Type:** Full Time  
**Reports To:** President

**About Ferry Cap**

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is a long-established American manufacturer of engineered fasteners and specialty metal components serving demanding industrial and power generation applications. As we invest in our people, equipment, and operating systems, we are seeking a senior quality leader who can help strengthen our processes and build a companywide culture of quality.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will lead Ferry Cap’s quality organization and serve as a key member of the company’s leadership team.

This is a hands on leadership position for someone with strong experience in metallurgy, metal transformation, manufacturing processes, and heat treatment. The successful candidate will work closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, supply chain, and customers to improve process control, solve technical problems, and ensure consistent product quality.

The right leader will view quality as an operating partnership, not simply an inspection function. This individual must be comfortable working on the production floor, engaging directly with employees, and helping build quality into every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all quality assurance, quality control, laboratory, inspection, and quality systems activities.
* Partner directly with operations to establish a culture in which safety, delivery, quality, and cost are shared responsibilities.
* Provide technical leadership related to metallurgy, raw materials, metal forming, metal transformation, machining, threading, and heat treatment.
* Oversee metallurgical testing and analysis, including hardness, microstructure, case depth, decarburization, mechanical properties, material certification, and failure analysis.
* Evaluate and improve heat treatment processes, including furnace controls, quenching, tempering, process consistency, and product conformance.
* Strengthen incoming, in process, and final inspection systems to ensure product requirements are consistently achieved.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action activities involving internal defects, customer complaints, supplier issues, and process failures.
* Use structured problem solving methods such as 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and MSA.
* Maintain and continuously improve the company’s quality management system, documentation, procedures, work instructions, and audit processes.
* Ensure compliance with customer requirements, industry standards, specifications, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Lead customer audits, supplier audits, internal audits, and customer quality reviews.
* Build strong working relationships with customer quality and engineering teams.
* Develop meaningful quality metrics, including first pass yield, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, corrective action effectiveness, and supplier performance.
* Improve material traceability and process control throughout the manufacturing operation.
* Lead supplier quality development and ensure purchased materials and outside processes meet Ferry Cap requirements.
* Develop, coach, and hold accountable the quality team while strengthening quality knowledge throughout the organization.
* Support new product introduction, process changes, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish clear containment, escalation, and corrective action processes when quality concerns arise.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant quality leadership experience in a metal manufacturing environment.
* Strong practical knowledge of metallurgy, material properties, metal transformation, and heat treatment.
* Experience with manufacturing processes such as cold forming, forging, machining, threading, rolling, or similar metalworking operations.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose metallurgical and manufacturing process failures.
* Experience leading quality systems, customer audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong working knowledge of dimensional inspection, mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, calibration, and measurement systems.
* Experience using quality tools such as PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis.
* Proven ability to work collaboratively with operations and engineering teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem solving skills.
* Willingness to spend significant time on the manufacturing floor and become personally involved in resolving issues.
* Bachelor’s degree in metallurgy, materials science, engineering, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant manufacturing experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including at least five years in a leadership role.
* Experience with engineered fasteners, high strength components, critical industrial products, or power generation applications.
* Experience with ISO based quality management systems and customer specific quality requirements.
* Experience working with commercial heat treat suppliers and internal heat treatment operations.
* ASQ certification, Six Sigma certification, or formal Lean manufacturing training.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.

**Leadership Profile**

The successful candidate will be:

* Hands on and comfortable working directly with production employees.
* Collaborative and capable of building trust across departments.
* Technically strong, practical, and decisive.
* Focused on preventing defects instead of relying on inspection to find them.
* Comfortable challenging existing practices while respecting Ferry Cap’s people and history.
* Able to balance customer requirements with operational realities.
* Committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and developing others.

**Why Join Ferry Cap**

This position offers the opportunity to play a major role in the continued transformation and growth of a historic American manufacturing company. The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will have direct access to company leadership, meaningful influence over operations, and the opportunity to build a quality culture that supports Ferry Cap’s customers, employees, and long term success.

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

existing_roles.description:
Twist Bioscience is seeking a Director, Protein Operations to lead high-throughput protein production and characterization within our Operations organization. You will run a high-throughput operation that runs seven days a week and lead a large, multi-level team that delivers purified, well-characterized antibodies and proteins to internal programs and external customers on time, at quality, and at cost. The ideal candidate pairs deep expertise in protein expression, purification, and characterization with the rigor to scale a production organization and the drive to automate it.

**Leadership and Operations**

* Lead a large protein production and characterization organization that operates seven days a week, including managers, supervisors, scientists, and associates.
* Own key performance indicators (KPIs) for quality, on-time delivery, turnaround time (TAT), capacity, and cost of goods sold (COGS), and model capacity and staffing against demand.
* Drive continuous process improvement and lead complex investigations, including customer incidents.
* Maintain SOPs, documentation, and training in line with ISO 13485 and other regulatory requirements.

**Protein Production**

* Oversee high-throughput antibody production in HEK293, CHO, and cell-free systems across IgG, Fab, scFv, VHH, and bispecific formats.
* Lead downstream purification of diverse biologics, including bispecific and engineered antibodies.
* Transfer new products and processes from R&D into production and support new product introductions (NPI).

**Protein and Antibody Characterization**

* Oversee Twist's binding, developability, and cell-based functional assay suite, from assay development through execution, analysis, and data reporting, with turnaround times as fast as 1–5 business days.
* Lead binding assessment, including flow cytometry on native antigen, single-point and full kinetics/affinity (KD) by SPR and BLI, and epitope binning by SPR and BLI.
* Lead developability profiling, including analytical size-exclusion chromatography (aSEC), thermostability (nanoDSF), size distribution (DLS), polyspecificity (BVP ELISA, ovalbumin off-target), self-interaction (AC-SINS), and hydrophobic interaction screening.
* Deliver high-quality, consistent datasets that support customer lead selection and AI/ML model training.

**Automation and Scale**

* Partner with Engineering to bring a high level of automation to production and characterization, translating workflows into requirements for liquid handling, robotics, scheduling, and data systems.
* Drive walk-away, high-throughput workflows integrated with LIMS, MES, and SAP to increase capacity, reduce turnaround time, and improve reproducibility.

**Collaboration**

* Partner with R&D, Process Development, Supply Chain, QC, QA, Project Management, and Customer Support to grow the portfolio and meet customer commitments.
* Shape technology and product direction with senior leadership while staying current on antibody discovery, protein expression, and lab automation.

### **What You'll Bring to the Team**

* PhD in protein biochemistry, biological chemistry, immunology, or a related field with 8+ years of experience in biotech, biopharma, or life science tools; or a BS/MS with 12+ years of equivalent experience.
* Experience managing managers and leading large teams, with strong coaching and people development skills.
* A proven track record of scaling protein or antibody production workflows and commercial products.
* Hands-on expertise in mammalian expression, purification (e.g., ÄKTA), and antibody characterization, including SPR/BLI kinetics and epitope binning, flow cytometry, and developability assays (aSEC, nanoDSF, DLS, AC-SINS, polyspecificity).
* Success partnering with engineering teams to implement automated, high-throughput lab workflows.
* Experience owning budgets, KPIs, and capacity planning, with working knowledge of ISO 13485/GMP, Lean, and Six Sigma.
* A strategic thinker who executes tactically, prioritizes well, and influences senior leadership.
* Excellent communication and presentation skills.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience running a high-throughput, made-to-order production operation in the life sciences.
* Experience manufacturing and purifying engineered antibodies.
* Experience with antibody characterization platforms such as Carterra and Octet.
* Familiarity with LIMS, MES, and ERP/SAP systems.

**About Twist Bioscience**

Twist Bioscience synthesizes genes from scratch, known as "writing" DNA. Just as children learn to both read and write, the next phase of development for the genomics revolution is the ability to write DNA.

At Twist Bioscience, we work in service of people who are changing the world for the better. In fields such as health care,agriculture, industrial chemicals and data storage, our unique silicon-based DNA Synthesis Platform provides precision at a scale that is otherwise unavailable to our customers.

existing_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
***Ready to lead a function, not just a shift? This is your next step.***

American Armor Gloves makes high-quality nitrile gloves here at home in South Carolina. Healthcare workers, first responders, and essential workers across the country rely on what we build. Our purpose is simple: **We strengthen America by building quality protection at home.**

We're a lean, growing manufacturer scaling toward 320–350 people, and we've spent the past year building the foundation for that growth: a redesigned organization, a clear vision with quarterly milestones, defined leadership roles, and a new leadership and compensation architecture. Manufacturing is the heart of that growth, and we need a leader ready to own it.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

The Director of Manufacturing is one of the most essential roles in our company. You'll own the end-to-end performance of our Manufacturing department, turning business plans into consistent, safe, high-quality production results.

This role is built for an accomplished Manufacturing Manager who is ready to take the next step. You've proven you can run a strong operation. Now you're ready to **lead through systems and leaders rather than personal effort on the floor**, and to build a manufacturing function that performs at a high level no matter which team is on shift.

Reporting to our VP of Operations, you'll be the bridge between enterprise strategy and shift-by-shift execution. You'll set the systems, build the leaders, and own the results.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* **Own manufacturing performance.** Deliver results across safety, quality, OEE, throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, scrap, and downtime through accountable leaders and strong systems.

* **Build repeatable production systems.** Design shift handoffs, accountability routines, labor deployment standards, and scheduling so performance never depends on heroics.

* **Lead and develop your Shift Manager team.** Coach your Shift Managers as leaders, not only as production operators, and build the next generation of manufacturing leadership.

* **Integrate compounding and batching.** Keep material availability, formulation compliance, and production demand aligned and well governed.

* **Drive continuous improvement.** Lead projects that reduce waste, improve workflow, raise OEE, and close performance gaps, in partnership with Process Engineering.

* **Partner across the business.** Work side by side with Quality, Process Engineering, Maintenance, Logistics, and People & Culture to remove barriers to production.

* **Build workforce capability.** Own training plans, manufacturing career pathways, and engagement so our workforce is ready to support growth.

**WHAT YOU'LL OWN**

You'll set daily and weekly production priorities, deploy labor across shifts, manage Shift Manager performance, and direct improvement projects within manufacturing. You'll shape manufacturing KPI targets, capacity planning, equipment needs, and staffing structure through your recommendations to the VP of Operations. You'll lead Shift Managers, Production Planning, and Batching/Compounding leadership, with a frontline team of Production Supervisors and Manufacturing Associates across multiple shifts.

**A REAL CAREER PATHWAY**

We grow leaders deliberately, and this role is designed as a launch point, not a ceiling. Our leadership framework defines exactly what it takes to grow from functional leadership into executive leadership, and we invest in getting high performers there.

* **Where you go next.** The Director of Manufacturing is a direct pathway to VP of Operations or other senior operations leadership, based on demonstrated enterprise judgment, cross-functional partnership, and the strength of the leadership bench you build.

* **How you get there.** Expect direct mentoring from the VP of Operations, exposure to enterprise planning and capital decisions, cross-functional visibility, and formal leadership development.

* **A clear standard.** Your growth is measured against the same competency framework used for job descriptions, performance reviews, and succession planning, so you always know where you stand and what comes next.

* **Visibility at the top.** Our annual bench-strength review puts strong leaders on the executive team’s radar early.

**WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW**

* **Essential to the mission.** Every glove we ship runs through the function you lead.

* **Build, not just run.** Our organization is lean and still forming, so you'll shape systems and standards that scale with the business.

* **A clear operating rhythm.** A shared vision, quarterly milestones, and a common scorecard keep leaders aligned and connect your work to company priorities.

* **Leave a legacy.** You'll develop Shift Managers into future Directors and Supervisors into future Shift Managers, building a team that carries the company forward.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Industrial Technology, Business, or a related field, or equivalent progressive leadership experience

* 8–10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership in a high-volume environment

* Proven success leading multiple shifts and developing frontline leaders

* A track record of owning department performance through KPIs, systems, and accountable leadership

* Strong cross-functional partnership with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and HR

* Solid knowledge of OSHA safety requirements and manufacturing quality systems

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, ERP/MRP systems (NetSuite preferred), KPI dashboards, production scheduling, and QMS

**Bonus points for:** experience in medical device, PPE, chemical processing, or FDA-regulated manufacturing; Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement practice; ERP implementation; and leading through growth and scale.

**HOW YOU LEAD**

You lead safely, every shift, not only when incidents happen. You hold leaders accountable through systems, not by stepping in for them. When something breaks, you fix the system, not just the shift. You raise problems early and directly. You treat Quality, Engineering, and Maintenance as partners, and you understand how manufacturing affects the entire business.

**READY FOR YOUR NEXT STEP?**

If you're a Manufacturing Manager ready to own a function, build leaders, and grow into enterprise leadership with a company that's scaling with purpose, we'd like to hear from you. Apply today.

This role is key to the daily management and continuous refinement of trade compliance related to return material authorization (RMA), repair, replacement, refurbishment, and service inventory movements. existing_roles.title: Regional Director of Operations
existing_roles.description:
At El Pollo Loco, we are on a mission to be the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant. When it comes to our people, we are all about growth. Whether that means specialized training, a clearly laid out career trajectory or collaborating cross-functionally, we are committed to the success of our people the same way we’ve been committed to the success of the El Pollo Loco brand for the last 50 years. In fact, we see you as our secret ingredient. While our chicken is fire, it’s our people who set us ablaze.
  
  
Our restaurants are only the tip of the flame! If you’re looking for an innovative, winning, and welcoming workplace, then a flamin’ good career in our Restaurant Support Center is right for you.
  
  
At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
  
  
Let’s Get Loco!
  
  
What’s in it for you!
  
  

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:**  
The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for driving El Pollo Loco’s success in the Los Angeles, CA region. They are responsible for providing operational expertise, strategic leadership and coaching. Directs, leads, manages and analyzes all aspects of the restaurant operations for the Areas under their direction to ensure achievement and maintenance of the regional sales, budgetary targets, controllable profit, performance metrics (e.g., service, quality, cleanliness, etc.), brand integrity, and compliance standards (e.g., food and restaurant safety, federal/state/local labor laws, etc.). Implements and executes strategic and tactical operational initiatives that support future business growth strategies. Oversees and manages adequate resource availability for existing and new restaurant openings including the attraction, retention, training, development and coaching of a high performing management team.
  
  
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* Oversees all aspects of the region’s restaurant business, operations, and facilities. Directs and aligns company strategies with restaurant management activities.
* Utilizes reporting systems to determine trends in sales, cost of goods and guest services. Reviews, monitors and manages the financial progress of the individual restaurants and region, including food and labor costs, ensuring budgeted targets are achieved.
* Meets regularly with Area Leaders to coach, develop, train and review performance, share best practices and disseminate information on any areas where there is an opportunity for improvement (e.g., P&L, RCP, FSA, QSC, Mystery Shops, etc.). Develops action plans with Area Leaders to improve revenue, profitability and quality/service standards.
* Directs, manages and ensures the region’s successful and timely implementation of all marketing strategies and LTOs. Supports and inspects marketing strategies in building guest counts and sales.
* Provides effective and timely resolution to all guest and employee complaints, conflicts and employee relations that cannot be resolved at the Area Leader level.
* Ensures the region’s restaurants are in compliance with all local, regional, and national laws and have all the required documentation and paperwork.
* Leverages two-way communication with Field and Support Center employees. Represents the Operations perspective on prioritization, planning and promotions to inspire operational excellence, effective implementation and facilitate insights. Provides specific operational input and feedback into the development of new products and programs to ensure successful execution.
* Collaborates with Development, Human Resources, and Operations in the coordination and execution of new restaurant openings. Directs team selection, monitors the training and ensures the teams perform to El Pollo Loco’s standards. Participates in the local public relations support in all locations. Approves employee relocation within region ensuring moves are conducted in the most economical and efficient manner.
* Develops regional succession plans: evaluates open opportunities, assesses internal talent, oversees management training programs, and drives recruiting efforts to ensure adequate number of managers are available to sustain growth of the organization.
* Champions effective vertical and horizontal communications within the regional area including Company-wide news of interest, upcoming events, new facilities, promotions, product developments, “Best Practices” among peers, etc. Prepares thoroughly and delivers well-organized, dynamic and informative presentations to senior management as needed. Holds meetings with their respective teams on a regular basis to ensure fluid and consistent messaging.
* Creates and fosters a positive team environment through recognizing and reinforcing behaviors and results that are aligned with El Pollo Loco’s core values and culture. Ensures open channels for employee suggestions.
* Interacts professionally and ethically, constructively participating as a collaborative team leader in pursuit of common goals, including active attendance to meetings. Initiates cost-effective suggestions to improve operational procedures.
* Other activities, duties or responsibilities that are assigned by your supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
  
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
  
  
**Education/Work Experience:**  
High school diploma or equivalent (GED) required, BA/BS degree in Business Administration preferred. 8+ years QSR/multi-site restaurant experience as an Area Leader or District Manager required; 5+ years regional QSR management experience preferred; 3+ years El Pollo Loco experience preferred; and a track record of success in leading, managing, coaching and developing high performance teams.
  
  
**License/Certifications:**  
Current valid driver’s license required as frequent weekly travel is involved. Current ServSafe certification preferred.
  
  
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**  

* Experience with successfully recruiting, building, and developing a team (based on current and future needs).
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives.
* Must be decisive and able to make fact-based decisions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners.
* Ability to prioritize and plan work assignments and work under pressure of frequent and tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex reports, documents, and correspondence.
* Adept at managing and prioritizing competing time sensitive requests while working well in a team atmosphere that may be under pressure.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significance to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Must be willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state restaurant locations, as needed by car or airplane.

Our Company
  
  
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. And today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide customers with fresh and innovative L.A. Mex from our famous family dinners to Mexican entrees.
  
  
The pay range identified is the hourly or salary rate El Pollo Loco expects to pay for the posted position. This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. Individual pay will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.

existing_roles.description:
**Relocation assistance is available for this position.**

**Who We Are**

Stored Energy Systems (SENS) is an award-winning manufacturer of premium quality power conversion products located in Longmont, CO. In business for over 50 years, SENS is the market leader with a proven track record of providing highly reliable battery chargers, DC power systems, and related products to industrial markets. For more information on our company please see our web site at www.sens-usa.com.

**View the SENS Product Catalog**

**Summary**

SENS is seeking a manufacturing engineering leader to help build and scale the organization, processes, and technical capabilities required for our next stage of growth. Supporting the expansion of existing manufacturing operations and establishing new operations at our Broomfield Systems manufacturing factory, this leader will establish the manufacturing engineering strategy, develop a multidisciplinary team, and translate business growth plans into manufacturing capacity and reliable production processes for our fastest-growing products.

This role leads manufacturing engineering, industrialization, tooling, test systems, automation, and technical production support for our systems products, with a strong emphasis on configure-to-order assembly manufacturing. Working closely with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, the Senior Manager will establish clear priorities, strengthen new product and production transfer readiness, and deliver measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and equipment reliability.

A successful candidate will combine organizational leadership with practical technical judgment, building a team that can support daily production while executing the improvements and investments needed to scale.

**Responsibilities**

* Help to build and develop the manufacturing engineering organization. Assess current capabilities, define the team structure and staffing plan, recruit talent, and develop engineers and technical leaders to support SENS’s growth.
* Establish performance measures and execution discipline. Set departmental goals, review project and operational performance, communicate risks and resource needs, and hold the team accountable for measurable improvements in manufacturing readiness, capacity, productivity, and equipment reliability.
* Establish and execute the manufacturing engineering roadmap. Translate business growth, product plans, and production requirements into prioritized initiatives for manufacturing capacity, processes, tooling, test systems, automation, and equipment reliability.
* Lead manufacturing readiness for new products and production transfers. Partner with Design Engineering, Production, Quality, and Planning & Fulfillment to establish readiness criteria and ensure processes, equipment, tooling, test capability, documentation, and training are in place before production release.
* Develop scalable manufacturing processes and standards. Establish consistent methods for process development, validation, work instructions, engineering changes, and production controls across manufacturing locations while accommodating product-specific requirements.
* Expand manufacturing capacity and improve productivity. Lead engineering efforts in capacity analysis, line balancing, factory layout, workflow, cycle-time reduction, and constraint elimination to support production demand and improve labor efficiency.
* Provide reliable technical support to Production. Establish clear support coverage, escalation processes, and problem-solving practices that resolve production issues promptly and prevent recurrence while maintaining progress on strategic projects.
* Guide manufacturing technology development. Lead technical specialists responsible for manufacturing test systems, production software, tooling, and automation. Prioritize investments based on safety, quality, capacity, reliability, and financial return.
* Improve production equipment reliability. Establish equipment ownership, maintenance strategies, critical spare requirements, and preventive and predictive maintenance practices in partnership with Production and technical support teams.
* Manage projects, capital investments, and departmental resources. Develop business cases, budgets, schedules, and resource plans; oversee implementation and production acceptance; and verify that projects deliver their expected operational and financial benefits.
* Partner with Design Engineering on manufacturability. Incorporate manufacturing feedback early in product development and engineering changes to improve assembly, testability, quality, serviceability, and cost.
* Drive safe processes and sustained quality improvement. Partner with EHS and Quality to incorporate risk assessment, error prevention, root cause analysis, and corrective action into manufacturing processes and equipment changes.
* Oversee the development and maintenance of manufacturing processes, work instructions, test procedures, tooling, fixtures, automation systems, and production software solutions.
* Be directly accountable for engineering project delivery, manufacturing readiness, equipment reliability, and validated improvement benefits, while sharing accountability with Production and Quality for labor efficiency and first-pass yield (FPY).

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline, or an additional 4 tears of manufacturing engineering experience.
* Eight or more years of experience in manufacturing engineering, production engineering, industrialization, or a related technical manufacturing role.
* Three or more years of experience directly leading engineering or technical teams, including setting priorities, developing employees, allocating resources, and managing performance.
* Demonstrated success improving manufacturing performance, with measurable results in productivity, capacity, quality, cost, or equipment reliability.
* Experience developing and improving manufacturing processes, tooling, fixtures, work instructions, and production controls, including introducing new or revised products into production.
* Ability to lead engineers and technical specialists across manufacturing processes, test systems, automation, and production support, using sound technical judgment to evaluate solutions and resolve issues.
* Practical application of Lean Manufacturing and structured problem-solving methods, including root cause analysis and corrective action.
* Experience leading cross-functional projects with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, balancing daily production needs with longer-term improvement priorities.
* Experience planning and executing manufacturing improvement or capital equipment projects, including defining scope, schedules, resource requirements, and expected business results.
* Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to translate business objectives into clear team priorities and communicate progress, risks, and decisions.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in manufacturing of configure-to-order (CTO) and engineered-to-order (ETO) electrical systems such as switchgear, switchboard, etc.
* Experience with manufacturing software development, automated test systems, and data acquisition platforms.
* Experience using ERP systems such as SyteLine for BOM management, item masters, engineering changes, and manufacturing planning.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent certification.
* Experience managing departmental budgets and capital equipment projects from business case through production acceptance.

**Location:** Longmont, CO

**Base Compensation:** $120,000 - $175,000 is the projected annual base salary range for this role and will be determined on the candidate’s overall qualifications and experience.

**Bonus:** This position is eligible for an annual bonus based on individual and company performance.

**Closing Date:** December 15th. While we expect to keep the position open through this date, the posting may be extended or closed early based on applicant volume and hiring needs.

**Onsite Perks**

* Free gym with 24/7 access
* Free Electric Vehicle charging
* Breakfast and Lunch Café
* After hours Grab & Go snacks
* Basketball court
* Walking paths

**Benefits**

* Paid Time Off
* Paid holidays
* Medical insurance
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability
* Life insurance
* 401(k) plan with immediate vesting
* Employee referral program
* Tuition reimbursement
* Professional development

At SENS, our culture is rooted in a set of core values that reflect who we are and how we work. In a recent 2025 poll, our employees identified the values that best define us: *“Innovative”, “Respectful”, “Inviting”, “Flexible”, “Collaborative”, and “Growth Driven”.* Our team describes us as a dynamic, forward-thinking company where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

We pride ourselves on being an equal opportunity employer, fully dedicated to fostering inclusion and diversity. We welcome all applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

We hope you're interested in making a difference with us. Even if you don't feel that you meet every qualification listed in this job description, we still encourage you to apply.

protected_roles.description:
Bio-Rad is seeking a Director of Manufacturing to lead our chemical manufacturing operations in Richmond, California, with additional responsibility for developing pilot manufacturing capabilities in Suzhou, China.
  
  
This role provides leadership across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, Quality Control, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety. The Director is accountable for delivering strong performance in safety, quality, customer service, cost, productivity, and inventory while building manufacturing capabilities to support future business growth.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring strong manufacturing and technical leadership, business judgment, and experience leading complex operations in a regulated environment. This position partners closely with Quality, EH&S, R&D, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, and business leadership to ensure reliable operations, successful new product introductions, and a resilient manufacturing network.
  
  
**How You’ll Make An Impact**

* Lead chemical manufacturing operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and customer service.
* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with business requirements, capacity needs, gross margin objectives, and long-term growth.
* Lead and develop a multidisciplinary organization across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, QC, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety.
* Drive operational excellence through Lean, Six Sigma, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with applicable quality, environmental, health and safety, chemical process safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with EH&S, Quality, Regulatory, Legal, and other functions to proactively identify and mitigate operational, regulatory, and business continuity risks.
* Develop and execute equipment, infrastructure, automation, and capital investment strategies to improve reliability, capacity, and efficiency.
* Drive cost and productivity improvements across labor, yield, scrap, waste, material usage, manufacturing variances, and inventory.
* Partner with R&D and business teams to enable effective new product introduction, scale-up, industrialization, and technology transfer.
* Lead development of pilot manufacturing capabilities in Suzhou to support new product introduction and greater flexibility across the manufacturing network.
* Develop manufacturing budgets and capital plans and ensure disciplined management of operating expenses and investments.
* Build organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, employee engagement, and development of strong leaders.
* Foster a culture of safety, quality, accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and customer focus.

**What You Bring**

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Life Sciences, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific or technical discipline required; Master’s degree or PhD preferred.
* Work Experience: 12+ years experience leading manufacturing operations in a regulated and technically complex environment, preferably within chemical, life science, diagnostics, pharmaceutical, or related industries.
* Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary manufacturing and technical teams.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing operations, quality systems, EH&S, process safety, and regulatory compliance.
* Strong financial and business acumen, including experience with manufacturing budgets, product costs, productivity, inventory, and capital investment.
* Experience leading operational improvement, capital, automation, capacity, or manufacturing transformation initiatives.
* Experience supporting new product introduction, scale-up, industrialization, and/or technology transfer.
* Demonstrated ability to identify and manage complex operational and business risks while maintaining continuity of supply.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, communication, and cross-functional leadership skills.
* Demonstrated ability to develop leaders and build high-performing teams.
* Experience working across functions and geographies in a global organization preferred.
* Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, 5S, SAP, or comparable manufacturing systems preferred.

**Location:**
This position must be based in
**Richmond, CA**
and requires the employee to be located within commuting distance of the office.
  
  
**Total Rewards Package:**
At Bio-Rad, we’re empowered by our purpose and recognize that our employees are as well. That’s why we offer a competitive and comprehensive Total Rewards Program that provides value, quality, and inclusivity while satisfying the diverse needs of our evolving workforce. Bio-Rad's robust offerings serve to enrich the overall health, wealth, and wellbeing of our employees and their families through the various stages of an employee’s work and life cycle.
  
  
**Benefits:**
We’re proud to offer a variety of options, including competitive medical plans for you and your family, free HSA funds, a new fertility offering with stipend, group life and disability, paid parental leave, 401k plus profit sharing, an employee stock purchase program, a new upgraded and streamlined mental health platform, extensive learning and development opportunities, education benefits, student debt relief program, pet insurance, wellness challenges and support, paid time off, Employee Resource Groups (ERG’s), and more!
  
  
**Compensation:**
The estimated compensation range for this position is posted. Actual compensation will be provided in writing at the time of offer and is based on several factors we believe fairly and accurately impact compensation, including geographic location, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and other job-related factors permitted by law. This position is eligible for a variable bonus, which is dependent upon achievement of your individual objectives and Company performance.
  
  
**Who We Are:**
For 70 years, Bio-Rad has focused on advancing the discovery process and transforming the fields of science and healthcare. As one of the top five life science companies, we are a global leader in developing, manufacturing, and marketing a broad range of high-quality research and clinical diagnostic products. We help people everywhere live longer, healthier lives. Bio-Rad offers a unique employee experience with collaborative teams that span the globe. Here, you are supported by leadership to build your career and are empowered to drive change that makes an impact you can see.
  
  
**EEO Statement:**
Bio-Rad is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer, and we welcome candidates of all backgrounds. Veterans, people with physical or mental disabilities, and people of all race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin and citizenship status are encouraged to apply.
  
  
**Agency Non-Solicitation:**
Bio-Rad does not accept agency resumes, unless the agency has been authorized by a Bio-Rad Recruiting Representative. Please do not submit resumes unless authorized to do so. Bio-Rad will not pay for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.
  
  
**Fraud Alert**
: Bio-Rad has received reports of individuals posing as Bio-Rad recruiters to obtain information, including personal and financial, from applicants. Beware of these fake "recruiters" and job scams. Click here for more information on this scam and how to avoid it.
